detail.text: Partial PR #762 closes the range n >= k^2 (take c' = min c 1/2) and leaves hole h_lt, the same statement with n < k*k. Aristotle (project 9e8d9ab2, 24 min) reported a proof of h_lt modulo one have: Hoheisel's theorem (exists theta<1 with a prime in (x, x+x^theta] for large x; BHP gives 0.525), which is not in the pinned Mathlib and cannot be avoided: the forbidden windows have length about k^(1-c), so Chebyshev-strength prime counts are too weak. Its argument: t = max(theta,1/2), c = (1-t)/4, j…

references.note: Proves g(k) > k^(1+c) for an absolute c > 0, where g(k) is the least n > k+1 with every prime factor of C(n,k) above k. Not read; the statement is as ELS 1993 and an earlier annex on erdos-1094--h3 quote it.

literature_proposed.summary: This node is the Ecklund-Erdős-Selfridge bound: if 2k <= n and C(n,k) has no prime factor <= k, then n > k^(1 + c) for large k. Published 1974 and not formalised. The filer has not read the proof; a translator should read EES 1974 first (three pages) and judge whether it is elementary (Sylvester-Schur style counting of prime powers in k! against the product (n-k+1)...n) before attempting it. Of the three ELS ranges this is the likeliest to be within reach.
